insights.headline: Central banks bought 39 tonnes of gold in August as MCX gold slid ₹1,500/10g in two days
insights.summary: Central banks added a net 39 tonnes of gold in August, led by China and Poland, keeping 2026 buying on pace for a strong year. Domestic gold and silver fell over the past two sessions as a firmer dollar and rising yields weighed, with MCX gold dipping about ₹1,500 per 10 grams. Traders now look to the RBI policy decision on October 7 and the US Fed for the next cue.
points: World Gold Council: central banks bought a net 39t of gold in August; China added 20t, its 22nd straight month of buying.
MCX gold slipped about ₹1,500/10g over two days as the dollar strengthened and bond yields climbed.
RBI is widely expected to raise the repo rate to 5.50% on October 7, its first hike since February 2023.
Deutsche Bank sees a possible silver surplus in 2027 as solar demand softens; 2026 is still a deficit year.
Jewellers report resilient festive demand around Dhanteras and Diwali despite record prices.

trending.title: Central banks keep accumulating gold
trending.summary: WGC's August data shows 39t of net buying led by China and Poland, and the LBMA 2026 narrative frames gold as a hedge against debt and currency debasement.

trending.title: Dollar and yields decide the near term
trending.summary: A firm dollar and climbing yields pushed gold and silver down on both COMEX and MCX, with analysts flagging key support and resistance levels to watch.

trending.title: Silver's two-sided story
trending.summary: Deutsche Bank warns a Chinese solar slowdown could flip silver into surplus by 2027, even as analysts see near-term support holding and Mexico's mine output weakens.

trending.title: A policy-heavy week for Indian buyers
trending.summary: The RBI's October 7 rate decision looms over gold, while the GST Council weighs tax parity on nominated agency gold imports.

trending.title: Festive demand holds up at record prices
trending.summary: Jewellers expect strong Dhanteras and Diwali buying, with jewellery stocks reflecting the retail mood, even as high prices push buyers toward lighter pieces.

items.title: Gold dips ₹1,500/10g in 2 days; silver off on strong dollar, 24-year-high yields
items.summary: MCX gold and silver opened lower on Tuesday as a firm US dollar and Treasury yields at 24-year highs weighed on the metals, though fading October Fed-hike bets capped losses. Gold has fallen ₹1,500 per 10g in two days; MCX December gold was at ₹1,49,901/10g and silver futures at ₹2,25,127/kg. Spot gold was down 0.3% at $4,128.69; silver off 0.6% at $60.67.

items.title: Central Bank Gold Statistics: Central banks continue summer spree in August
items.summary: World Gold Council data shows central banks made net gold purchases of 39 tonnes in August, keeping 2026 buying on pace. China led with 20 tonnes in its 22nd consecutive month of buying, followed by Uzbekistan and Poland; year-to-date net purchases total 170 tonnes.

items.title: Gold inches lower as firmer dollar, higher yields weigh
items.summary: Gold eased on Tuesday as a firm US dollar and Treasury yields at 24-year highs weighed on the metal. Spot gold slipped 0.3% to $4,128.69 an ounce and US gold futures were flat at $4,156.00, with losses limited as expectations of an October Fed hike faded after weak September jobs data. Traders still price an 87% chance of a hike in December. Spot silver fell 0.6% to $60.67.

items.title: RBI widely seen raising repo rate to 5.50% on Oct 7, first hike since Feb 2023
items.summary: The RBI's six-member monetary policy committee meets Oct 5-7, with the decision due Wednesday. Markets and economists widely expect a 25-basis-point hike to 5.50% - the first since February 2023 - after four holds. Drivers: Brent crude above the $90/bbl August-policy assumption, CPI at 4.82% in August, and global tightening; some see another hike in December.
points: MPC meets Oct 5-7; decision due Wednesday 10 am IST, per RBI's published calendar.
Markets widely expect a 25bp hike to 5.50%, the first since February 2023.
Drivers: Brent above the $90/bbl August assumption, CPI at 4.82% in August, global tightening.
Some economists see another 25bp hike in December if crude stays elevated.
Higher rates typically headwind gold; a stronger rupee could trim domestic premiums.

items.title: LBMA 2026: Gold is sending a message as debt fears fuel the debasement trade
items.summary: Market experts at the LBMA's annual Global Precious Metals Conference said gold's resilience despite soaring bond yields is itself a message: investors are pricing in unsustainable government debt and the erosion of fiat currencies.
points: Nippon India MF's Vikram Dhawan: global debt rising by trillions yearly leaves governments with financial repression — higher inflation, capped borrowing costs.
TRS of Texas's Shayne McGuire: investors increasingly worry growing debt will erode the value of money, reviving the debasement motive for gold.
The panel, moderated by MKS PAMP's Nicky Shiels, argued the old rulebook — surging yields kill gold — no longer holds.

items.title: Silver shortage could flip to surplus in 2027: Deutsche
items.summary: Deutsche Bank expects rising inventories and weaker industrial demand to flip silver into surplus as early as 2027, with spot averaging $70/oz in the second quarter of 2027 - below early-2026 levels. 'Peak silver scarcity is clearly in the rear-view mirror,' analyst Daniel Ghali said. Silver traded near $61 early Monday, down about 14% this year but up roughly 26% from a year ago.

items.title: Gold, silver outlook: Key support, resistance levels; triggers to watch
items.summary: Anuj Gupta, research analyst, says gold and silver are consolidating in a range after last week's profit booking. He puts MCX gold supports at ₹1,48,500/₹1,47,700 and resistance at ₹1,50,000/₹1,50,800; MCX silver supports at ₹2,22,000/₹2,18,000 per kg, resistance ₹2,28,000/₹2,32,000. Key triggers: Fed minutes and the Oct 27-28 FOMC meeting, the dollar index, and bond yields.

items.title: Gold price suffers under oil, yield pressures, Mexico's silver production weakens in July – Heraeus
items.summary: Gold broke through $4,250/oz support last week as multi-decade-high bond yields, a stronger dollar and Brent near $100 overwhelmed buying interest, Heraeus analysts wrote, leaving the year-to-date lows near $4,000 as next support. They also flagged weak July silver output in Mexico, the world's largest producer.
points: The 10-year Treasury yield climbed above 5.3%, its highest since 2002, lifting the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding gold.
Brent near $100 a barrel is reinforcing fears that energy costs keep inflation elevated and policy tight for longer.
For silver, Mexico — the world's largest producer — posted weak July output, a supply-side counterpoint to demand-weakness calls.

items.title: Silver (XAG/USD) Price Forecast: $59.69 Support Holds Key to Recovery
items.summary: Spot silver is at a decision point around $59.69, analyst Bruce Powers wrote: a sustained break below turns the near-term outlook bearish, while a rally above last week's $64.11 high would signal buyers regaining control. A bearish 20/50-day moving-average crossover points to weakening momentum.

items.title: Gold imports by nominated agencies may come under GST as Council weighs tax parity
items.summary: The GST Council will meet on October 8 to consider bringing gold imports by nominated agencies such as MMTC and STC under GST, aligning their tax treatment with imports routed through banks. Currently only banks pay 3% GST on gold imports.

items.title: MCX Evening Update: Gold and Silver futures see moderate gains
items.summary: MCX gold futures for October 2026 edged up 0.57% to Rs 1,44,105 per 10 grams in the evening session, testing highs above Rs 1,44,300. Silver futures rose 0.42% to Rs 2,18,151 per kg amid a modest rise in open interest.

items.title: Gold falls nearly 1%, silver gains on MCX: What is driving bullion prices
items.summary: MCX gold futures slipped about 1% — Rs 1,020 per 10g — to Rs 1.49 lakh as the US dollar climbed to an 18-month high of 102.37 and Treasury yields stayed elevated, while silver rose 0.54% (Rs 1,223/kg) to Rs 2.27 lakh per kg; international spot gold held steady near $4,163.50 an ounce.

items.title: Festive season outlook: Jewellers expect strong buying despite changing consumer patterns
items.summary: CNBC-TV18 reports jewellers expect strong festive and wedding-season buying even as high gold prices change how consumers buy: lighter, lower-carat, versatile pieces within defined budgets, traction for old-gold exchange, and more room for diamonds. CRISIL sees 20-25% revenue growth for organised retailers this fiscal.

items.title: Titan, Kalyan Jewellers, PC Jeweller shares shine - Why jewellery stocks are glittering? Expert decodes rally
items.summary: Shares of Indian jewellery retailers rallied on Monday on hopes of strong festive-season sales. Kalyan Jewellers led with a 4.5% gain while Titan and PC Jeweller rose about 1.5%. Bonanza analyst Abhinav Tiwari said the market is positioning ahead of Dhanteras and Diwali.
